$comment: Global economy constants from design doc §8. All first-pass values — tune in Phase 3 against pacing targets.

costGrowth.$note: almanac is the geometric step on a REPEATABLE Almanac line (see almanac.json). A repeatable line is a sink, never a gate, which is the only reason an exponential cost is safe here: its benefit is additive per level (linear) against a cost that is exponential, so it tapers forever without ever walling. Gates must scale at most linearly with the fold count — see rites.json's demandGrowth note for why.

gifts.$note: design §4: gift piles — one pile earned per verse sung (lifetime, across Migrations), one yes each. pileGoods units of the node's OWN resource (§13: you leave a pile of what the flock likes), spent from camp stock at the node the player chooses; the arrival is that resource's specialist species (derived from species.json traits — no per-event species config) and takes the node as its post. A pile is refused where the specialist already walks or no specialist exists. pileGoods is a first guess.

delivery.$note: hauling as a throughput system is retired (it raced two absolute rates - gather vs carry - whose growth lanes could never be kept level, and any tuning was wrong for either a 4- or a 6-slot kith). Goods now reach camp automatically and losslessly: each node's pickings pool up and land as one batch every batchSeconds. The cadence exists ONLY so design S5 quality rolls stay per-batch (never per unit) and Pristine keeps landing as a discrete windfall - it is not a cap, and nothing gathered is ever lost.

kith.$note: design §4 ladder: a slot is the right to hold a post; companions past the slots rest at camp. One slot from minute one; one more as lifetime verses sung (across Migrations) cross each verseMilestones entry (first guesses); the last two are store purchases (the starter bundle, then the plain slot product) — slotsBase + milestones + 2 purchasable must equal slotsMax. generatorGatherPosts is what the Rite generator assumes a plausible kith can hold at gather nodes at once (run-2+ rites; earned and purchased slots are never assumed beyond it). gatherPerSecond is a familiar's base gather rate at its post (was an implicit 1.0) — cut to 0.1 on 2026-07-31 when hauling retired, because lossless deliveries roughly x4-5'd effective camp income; absent or 0 in hand-built data means 1.0.

crafting.$note: first-guess Phase-3 number, not in design doc — seconds per craft at every station before craftSpeedMult upgrades divide it. Tune against the §2 pacing targets (first recipe cooked ~20 min).

tools.$note: flint is knapped (no forge); each later tier also consumes an ingot batch (see recipes). deepsteel is the §5 'deep ores' tier past steel — smelted from the Hollows' deep-ore seams

mastery.$note: curve and xpPerUnit are first guesses, not in the design doc — mastery XP per unit gathered at the node, rung r costs base·growth^r. yieldBonusPerLevel applies to both yield and the raw resource's sell value (§4 '+5% yield/value').

verdure.$note: renownDivisor tuned via the balance model (docs/economy-model.xlsx, ECO-2 Renown) to bank ~10 Verdure at the first fold once Renown-at-fold rose with gatherPerUnit=3. Verdure = floor((lifetimeRenown / renownDivisor) ^ exponent). Model-derived; confirm in playtest.

xp.$note: gatherPerUnit tuned to 3 via the balance model (docs/economy-model.xlsx) so gathering pulls roughly even with familiar time-XP as a Renown source (§9 'every good handled credits Renown') — at 1 it was only ~22% of Renown. Note this also credits warden gathering-skill XP, but recipe gates (max level 5) are already met in minutes at any value, so progression is unaffected. craftPerBatch is still a first guess. Confirm in playtest.

quality.$note: design §5: quality rolls per delivery batch (Common 96% / Fine ~3.5% +50% value / Pristine 0.5% base). pristineValueMult is a first guess — the 'windfall' sale isn't priced in the doc. pristineChance = (pristineBaseChance + owned pristineChanceBonus effects) * (1 + tending.pristineChanceBonus while the node's tend window is live) — flat bonuses add points, Tending multiplies (§8).

amber.$note: Amber (design §10): the premium currency's free earn + soft sink. Site finds roll per tick at watchers * digFindsPerHour * digSpeedMult (a separate channel from field sketches — a fully-recorded site keeps surfacing amber; it's old resin with an ancient insect in it, the one thing takeable); a time-skip instantly credits timeSkipHours of full live production for timeSkipCostAmber. timeSkipDailyCapHours bounds PAID skips to that many skipped hours per real day (a leaky budget refilling at cap/24 per wall hour, so it holds on every timescale, no midnight cliff; 0/absent = uncapped). At 24 it pins a heavy spender to at most x2 a free player's pace: a day holds 24 natural sim-hours and skips may add at most 24 more — sim-time is the only thing money buys here, so this one number IS the whale throttle. The rewarded-ad skip sits OUTSIDE the budget (free players get it too — it's part of the baseline both sides share). adDripAmber is the small pile a rewarded ad gives; weeklyCacheAmber is the once-a-week Play Games cache (design §11). renameCostAmber is the small resin a familiar's rename asks — the arrival naming too, unless you keep the suggested name. All first guesses against the ~40/week-free lean.

store.$note: real-money catalogue constants. The starter bundle (Play Level Up's initial purchase offer) grants a kith slot plus this one-time pile of Amber; the plain kith_slot product grants the sixth slot alone. The amber packs (amber_pack_small/large) are consumable buy-amber products granting these piles. Amounts are first guesses (starter ~2 time-skips; small pack ~3, large ~10).

observation.$note: design §6 (observe · sketch · release). sketch rate = watchers * baseSketchesPerHour * digSpeedMult upgrades * the site's summed unrecorded rarity, rolled per tick; a field sketch is guaranteed once pityTimerHoursWatched hours of watching pass without one. baseSketchesPerHour is a first guess — tune so the first insect plate completes inside the MVP playtest. `skill` is the craft the watching trains — Observation in the design doc (§5), `entomology` in the data — and watchXpPerHour credits it per watcher per site-hour, scaled by the site's dig-speed multiplier. The XP is paid for the WATCHING, not the sketch: sketches are a finite lifetime pool (25 across every plate) that rides the fold in insectSketches while skillXp resets, so a per-sketch award would leave a fully-recorded run unable to level this skill at all — and Brush Screens (entomology 8) unbuyable forever. At 50 a lone wanderer clears the level-8 gate in ~19 site-hours (~10 with two sites open), so the screens arrive while there are still plates left to be worth doubling.

tending.$note: burst values are first guesses — tune in Phase 1.

bubbles.$note: windfall bubbles — the active-play reward that replaced tap-to-tend. A worked node floats a bubble up the strip every spawnIntervalSec (at most maxLive adrift at once, each living lifetimeSec); catching one grants rewardRatePerSecond x rewardSeconds of that node's resource straight to camp AND tends the node (burst + Pristine window + Rite tend deed). lifetimeSec deliberately exceeds spawnIntervalSec so windfalls BANK — glancing away banks 2-3 to pop in a burst instead of silently losing each one, and maxLive is the real ceiling. The haul is FLAT (2026-07-31): it used to be rewardSeconds of the node's OWN live output, which paid 1-2 units at most nodes — an unstaffed node earns only the wandering warden's share (warden.gatherPerSecond / node count), so the windfall shrank every time a zone opened, and the 2026-07-31 kith.gatherPerSecond cut to 0.1 took another 10x out of the staffed ones. rewardRatePerSecond is the notional gatherer behind the windfall, set to the warden's own hands so a catch reads as 'a minute of picking at that node' wherever it lands. Which nodes drift a bubble is still earned (someone must work it); only the size is fixed. Note a flat haul does not ride the late-game yield multipliers, so re-check its weight against zone 6-8 income in playtest.

warden.$note: first guess. The warden's own hands at their post (the last-tended node) — always on, boosted by a live burst, straight to camp stock. It's the early-game kickstart (assignment, not a tap surge) AND how a bare node earns its first own-resource replant (design §3), so it must stay positive.

familiarXp.$note: design §4: familiar run XP + Kinship. famXPToLevel(L) = base·growth^L (60·1.12^L), a powerup choice every 5 levels. xpPerSecond = base run XP a stationed familiar earns per second at its post; a wanderer earns half (§2). At Migration run XP converts to Kinship: kinshipGain = floor(√(runXP / kinshipDivisor)); each Kinship level gives +kinshipXpRatePerLevel XP rate and a higher starting level. Levels never scale output. kinshipDivisor tuned to 12000 via the balance model (docs/economy-model.xlsx) — a familiar stationed a whole run banks ~2 Kinship at the first fold; at 1000 it banked ~7. signatureMilestones = the Kinship levels where a familiar's signature deepens (§4's milestone lever): its species trait sharpens by signatureDeepening per milestone (trait value × (1 + 0.25·passed)) and its plate takes an inscription line (§7, species.json). At ~2 Kinship per well-worked fold: first signature around fold 1–2, second around fold 3, third deep in the seasons — first guesses, tune with the fold pacing. The rest are first guesses; postMatch/comfort multipliers (§8) are a later refinement (todo.md).

replant.$note: design §3: replanting a node's own resource raises its richness — the fourth output lane. replantCost(L) = baseCost·growth^L units of the node's OWN resource, spent from camp stock, per node per run; each level adds richnessPerLevel to the node's base yield (richnessMult = 1 + richnessPerLevel·level). No Renown — it pays back in yield, not the ledger. The warden's post trickle self-funds a virgin node's first replant (§3). Richness resets at Migration (except the Almanac's First Planting — a later slice). All first guesses.
